name: Generative Bionics GENE.01
summary: A bipedal humanoid from Genoa, Italy, with a full-body tactile skin for safe contact with workers; a welding variant for Fincantieri shipyards is planned for on-site testing in late 2026.

germany.statusNote: Working prototype shown in July 2026; no shipped commercial units, price or European sales route published.

specs.label: Body sensing
specs.value: full-body tactile skin (touch, force, temperature, proximity)

specs.label: Welding variant
specs.quote: the GENE.01/W variant, a specialized humanoid welder designed to operate inside the tight, ergonomically challenging environments of naval shipyards

specs.label: Digital twin
specs.value: open-sourced via PyPI, conda-forge and ROS
specs.quote: Generative Bionics is open-sourcing the robot’s digital twin across PyPI, Conda, and ROS ecosystem repositories

specs.label: Actuation
specs.value: European actuation stack co-developed with Synapticon
specs.quote: the startup has partnered with German actuation specialist Synapticon to co-develop an EU-protected actuation stack tailored to GENE.01

notes: Humanoids Daily lists GENE.01 as bipedal; its photos show five-finger hands.
Lower-body prototypes walked and ran on uneven outdoor terrain in May 2026; no rough-ground rating for the full robot.
No official height, weight, DOF, payload or runtime published.

images.alt: GENE.01 humanoid standing, full body, on a dark stage

evidence.task: Humanoid welding trials at Fincantieri's Sestri Ponente shipyard (GENE.01/W variant)
evidence.note: Four-year partnership signed February 2026; trials targeted for the end of 2026, not yet reported as started.

sources.title: Generative Bionics Unveils GENE.01: A Smart-Skin Humanoid Built on Peer-Reviewed Ergonomics
The Humanoids of Europe: Built by Their Customers

openQuestions: The maker site answered our crawler with HTTP 403, so no official spec sheet was read.
